div.div:
BUFFER RETENTION CONSTRAINTS (ASM-074, ASM-076, ASM-079):
- Field Telemetry: Non-volatile ring buffer. Sized with margin (>=30 readings). Max retention 24 hours.
Readings older than 24 h without ACK are evicted; local drop_counter is incremented.
- Transporter Phone Outbox: 7 days capacity (2,016 fixes). Custody events are NEVER evicted.
- Logistics Post: Encrypted outbox. Reception events held until persistence ACK. Zero data loss.

RELEASE CONTRACT: A record leaves the local buffer ONLY when verified cloud ACK is received.
If session drops mid-drain, remaining records stay and drain resumes at next reconnect.

div.div:
PART 1 CONTRACT SUMMARY — OFFLINE BEHAVIOR & PROTOCOL PROPERTIES:
1. Store-and-Forward: Max 24 h retention for farm & wet mill telemetry (ASM-074). Unacknowledged records >24 h evicted with gap report.
2. Transporter Outbox: 7 days capacity (2,016 fixes at 5 min interval). Custody events are never evicted; oldest fixes thinned to 15 min if full.
3. Drone Buffer: Storage on drone & ground station has NO time limit. Fumigation cannot close until flight record is persisted in cloud.
4. Replay Ordering: LIVE reading taken at reconnect published FIRST (never waits behind history); then buffered history drains OLDEST FIRST.
5. Release on ACK: Record released ONLY after MQTT PUBACK, HTTP 2xx, or verified S3 multipart checksum. Lost ACK causes safe duplicate.
6. Idempotency: Cloud stores keyed by (node_id + reading_timestamp) or UUID event_id. Duplicate delivery is harmlessly deduped.

div.div:
OBSERVABILITY OF SILENT NODES (Case Point 6 & A21):
Nodes and farms silent for more than 24 hours are detected by CloudWatch metric alarms and reported in daily operational dashboard.
Drained alerts are measured against the 24-hour limit, keeping the live <5 minute SLO unpolluted by buffer drains.

div.div:
CROP ALERT LATENCY BUDGET TABLE (docs/connectivity.md Section 8.2):
Hop 1: Reading taken to message ready on node Target: 10 s | Cumulative: 10 s | Node publishes immediately; no local evaluation
Hop 2: Radio wake, network attach and TLS connection Target: 60 s | Cumulative: 70 s | Multi-network SIM attaches to best available carrier
Hop 3: MQTT publish to PUBACK at IoT Core endpoint Target: 20 s | Cumulative: 90 s | QoS 1 with PUBACK; absorbs transient retransmissions
Hop 4: Topic rule to threshold function invocation Target: 10 s | Cumulative: 100 s | Routing rule through SQS threshold queue
Hop 5: Threshold function evaluation & persistence Target: 20 s | Cumulative: 120 s | Evaluates ranges, persists DynamoDB, dispatches SNS
Hop 6: Alert topic to notification channel provider Target: 30 s | Cumulative: 150 s | Amazon SNS HTTPS dispatch to Push/SMS gateway
Hop 7: Channel provider to farmer's smartphone Target: 60 s | Cumulative: 210 s | Push notification or SMS delivered to farmer phone
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total Design Target: 210 s (3.5 min) | Safety Margin: 90 s | Case Statement Hard Limit: 300 s (<5 minutes, Case Point 3)

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1742px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1900px; margin-left: 1861px;

div.div:
TRACEABILITY TO A21 ALERT-DELIVERY SLO (docs/connectivity.md Section 8.3 & Roadmap #34):
- Proposed SLI: Share of out-of-range readings published live (not from buffer) whose notification arrives on farmer phone within 300 s.
- Trace Points: 1. Reading timestamp (Hop 1) | 2. Broker PUBACK (Hop 3) | 3. Lambda execution start & alert persist (Hop 5) | 4. SNS handoff (Hop 6) | 5. Delivery receipt (Hop 7).
- Hop timestamps allow A21 to attribute any SLO breach to the exact failing hop (field attach vs cloud queue vs carrier SMS).
- Drained readings (offline buffer) are measured separately against the 24-hour limit; drying alerts use the identical budget.
